author: human
request:
Feature request: filter the vet list by specialty. Three product decisions
come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-9 is narrowed: free-text veterinarian search stays out of
  scope, but filtering the directory by an attribute it already shows is in.
  Record the narrowing the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The JSON endpoint at /vets is reinstated as a supported surface — this
  filter is its first requested capability. Mint a fresh requirement for it;
  the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused.
- The filter is a URL contract only. Neither surface gains a form, dropdown,
  or other page control in this request; pagination links carry the
  parameter so filtered pages stay navigable. A visible control may come as
  a follow-up request.

Both vet list surfaces accept an optional `specialty` query parameter:

- /vets.html?specialty=<name> — the HTML page shows only vets holding that
  specialty; pagination applies to the filtered list.
- /vets?specialty=<name> — the JSON endpoint returns only those vets.

Matching is on the whole specialty name, case-insensitive — not a prefix. A
specialty matching no vet yields the normal page or JSON document with an
empty vet list (HTTP 200). An empty or whitespace-only value behaves as if
the parameter were absent, like the empty owner search. Without the parameter
both endpoints behave as today. Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The filter lives entirely in the vet feature package, which already owns its entities, repository, controller, and template (system-design.md § Package Structure). Three things are new ground rather than a reuse of an existing pattern. First, a read that filters across the Vet-Specialty many-to-many with paging: owner search filters a scalar column, so the collection-join shape has no precedent here. Second, the caching decision: both VetRepository reads carry @Cacheable("vets") and that cache has no eviction and no size limit, so a read keyed by caller-supplied text cannot join them; the departure is recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-16-uncached-specialty-filtered-vet-reads.md and is required by architecture-principles.md § Consistency over novelty. Third, paging links that carry a reflected request parameter, which the owner list does not do. The REQ-VET-003 / REQ-VET-004 split does NOT change the implementation shape of this slice: REQ-VET-003 needs no production code at all — /vets already returns the vets and specialties the page lists, and reinstating it is a durable-memory status change (its Known Defects row is withdrawn, its Contracts rows now name it). REQ-VET-004 is the only code-bearing half, and it lands on both surfaces in one pass. Treat the slice as one behavior across two representations, not two units of work.
integration_points: VetRepository gains two filtered reads: a paged one for /vets.html and an unpaged Collection one for /vets. The JSON route uses findAll() today, so it needs the unpaged variant rather than a page.
Neither new repository method carries @Cacheable. The two existing reads keep their annotation untouched.

Matching is case-insensitive in the query (Spring Data IgnoreCase, i.e. upper() on both sides), not by column collation. This is the deliberate avoidance of the PostgreSQL divergence recorded in system-design.md § Known Defects for owner search; an H2-only test suite would not catch a collation-based implementation.

VetController binds specialty as an optional String on both handlers, normalizes null-or-blank to no filter, and selects the filtered or unfiltered repository call. The whole-name, case-insensitive matching rule stays in the query, not the controller.
The controller puts the normalized specialty on the model so vetList.html can rebuild paging hrefs with it.

vetList.html builds every paging href through Thymeleaf link-expression parameters (@{/vets.html(page=..., specialty=...)}) instead of the current string-concatenated __${}__ preprocessing. The parameter form URL-encodes the value; the concatenated form does not.
No new user-facing text on either surface, so no message-bundle keys change. Adding a label would oblige all eleven locales under REQ-LANG-002.

patterns.description: the project's filtered-paged repository read: a derived query method taking the filter value plus a Pageable, no explicit @Query
the sanctioned blank-parameter normalization: null or blank collapses to the broadest read, done at the controller as request adaptation
the existing vet pagination helper the filtered path extends; page size stays a local, per system-design.md § Constants
the caching departure and its consequences

risks.risk: A join fetch on the filtered association would return each vet carrying only the matched specialty, silently breaking the criterion that the machine-readable form carries the same specialties the page lists.
risks.mitigation: Filter through a plain join (or the derived IgnoreCase method) and let the existing EAGER @ManyToMany load the full specialty set. Assert in a test that a filtered vet holding two specialties still reports both.

risks.risk: A collection join multiplies rows, so an unguarded paged query can report duplicate vets and a wrong total.
risks.mitigation: Use Distinct in the derived method name. If the generated count query misbehaves under paging, fall back to an explicit @Query with a matching countQuery rather than filtering in memory.

risks.risk: Copying the neighbouring method signature drags @Cacheable("vets") onto the filtered read, making cache keys a function of untrusted request text in a cache with no eviction and no size limit.
risks.mitigation: The new methods carry no cache annotation. The ADR and the Threat Model row state it; a reviewer checks the annotation is absent.

risks.risk: The slice req_id REQ-VETSSPECIALTYFILTER-001 is not a PRD requirement id, so `grading.py contracts-sync --feature REQ-VETSSPECIALTYFILTER-001` fails on both docs and cannot be made to pass by any legitimate design-doc edit.
risks.mitigation: Run the gate check against the PRD ids this slice implements: contracts-sync --feature REQ-VET-003 and --feature REQ-VET-004 both pass as of this record. Do not inject the slice id into docs/system-design.md to satisfy the string match; the PRD half is the product expert's to record if the harness wants the slice id traceable.

risks.risk: The blank-to-absent normalization could be read as a new business rule in a controller, which architecture-principles.md § Validation Checklist forbids outright.
risks.mitigation: Keep it to null-or-blank collapsing, identical in shape to OwnerController:97-104, and keep the matching semantics in the repository query. A helper method named for normalization, not for matching, makes the split visible.

notes: Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records in the log, skipped. Durable memory written this dispatch: (1) docs/adr/2026-08-16-uncached-specialty-filtered-vet-reads.md, new ADR for the caching departure; (2) docs/adr/README.md index rows for that ADR and for the non-goal ADR the product expert left unindexed; (3) docs/system-design.md — a specialty-filter paragraph under Contracts, Implements columns for Vets/VetRepository/VetController updated to REQ-VET-003 and REQ-VET-004, the machine-readable-route row withdrawn from Known Defects with a replacement statement, the XSS threat row extended to the reflected specialty in paging links, a new unbounded-cache-growth threat row, and Open Question 5 amended. Residual questions, narrowest reading taken per the owner's standing constraint and recorded rather than escalated: a request naming the specialty more than once binds the first value and is not otherwise specified — no multi-value semantics are designed in; a specialty value of any length is safe unbounded because it is a bound query parameter and is no longer a cache key, so no length cap is introduced; the visible control stays out, so the model attribute exists solely to rebuild paging hrefs and is not rendered as text. Two edges worth a test that the acceptance list leaves implicit: a specialty held by a vet who holds others must still list all of them, and the JSON surface must be exercised with the parameter absent to prove the unfiltered path is untouched. Both are already covered by the prd-entry test names if written to assert the full specialty set.
